counterfactual_rationale: A speculative draft model wrote routed-expert captures into the target model's global buffer, diverging from the target-only baseline. Only a speculative MoE run with return_routed_experts enabled would plausibly expose the cross-runner contamination.

The ROCm gfx950 software fp8 conversion mishandled values in the top e4m3 exponent range and biased rounding. Boundary-value fp8 conversion tests on gfx950, especially values near 256-448 after scaling, would plausibly catch it.

With VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT enabled, DeepSeek-V3 serving hit a FlashAttention MLA scheduler_metadata shape RuntimeError. A batch-invariant serving/bench smoke test through FlashAttention MLA would plausibly reproduce the bad metadata shape.

The compile pass enabled a SiluMul+Nvfp4Quant fusion even when the custom op was unavailable, breaking compile tests with an unsupported fusion assertion. CI across build images with and without that op would plausibly catch the gating error.

The xFormers multi-query attention path mishandled ALiBi bias dimension expansion in an untested scenario. A reference attention test combining multi-query KV and ALiBi bias would plausibly expose the dimension bug.

The CPU extension failed to build on Apple M1 because x86-specific FP16 vector types and flags leaked into that architecture. Apple/ARM build coverage for the CPU kernels would plausibly catch this before merge.

The FA3 EAGLE draft-decode metadata scattered too-wide cache_loc data into a too-narrow page_table for topk > 1 and page_size > 1, corrupting memory. A memcheck or bounds-asserted test of that page-size/top-k combination would plausibly fail at the scatter.

The Triton DCP prefill path inferred a local GQA mapping after KV replication, corrupting Qwen3.5 DCP accuracy. Layout tests varying TP/DCP shards and comparing to the global GQA mapping would plausibly catch it.

Custom ops rejected SymInt dimensions or ScalarType objects under Dynamo dynamic shapes, blocking dynamic-shape quantization paths. Compile coverage of representative custom-op kernels under dynamic shapes would plausibly expose the integration failure.

The fused SiluMul+NVFP4 quant kernel used an approximate sigmoid and only online lm_eval exposed a slight accuracy drop. Tests with realistic activation distributions and precision-sensitive evals would plausibly reveal the approximation error.

The Triton GDN prefill conv1d kernel mixed fp16 activations with a bf16 conv-state cache, causing a branch phi dtype compile error. Unit coverage that varies x and cache dtypes would plausibly catch the mismatch before a full MiniCPM-V serve.

The fused KDA verify kernel wrote shared conv state from only one V tile, so later waves could read overwritten history and outputs varied with CTA scheduling. Re-running with constrained SMs or varied scheduling would plausibly expose the race.

The FP8 CUTLASS group GEMM backend was selected on SM120 even though implementations existed only for SM90 and SM100, yielding an unsupported-kernel error. Hardware-matrix CI including SM120 would plausibly catch the backend gate.

Sparse MLA mixed-batch routing could let req_id_per_token exceed the top-k tensor and write out of bounds, alongside packed FP8 gather metadata issues. Memcheck or bounds-checked tests for mixed decode/dense-prefill FP8 paths would plausibly flag it.

The NPU path had Gemma multimodal batch>1 page-alignment issues plus an NPU GemmaRMSNorm/Phi-3 accuracy fix. Ascend/NPU CI with those model and batch configurations would plausibly expose the failures.

The FA4 QV varlen decode path was incorrect for bs>1 and incompatible with the packed tile ratio for GLM TP1. Attention reference tests varying batch size and Q/KV head ratios would plausibly reveal the cross-sequence KV reads.
The record mentions Nightly GSM8K CI and FlashInfer kvcache quant but gives no error, root cause, or before/after behavior. I could not confidently determine the specific kernel-correctness failure.

New Mamba requests with a one-token budget could be scheduled as decode and read stale SSM cache state, producing gibberish. A serving test that stresses token-budget exhaustion and cache-slot reuse would plausibly catch the corruption.

The record describes fixing a broken CPU compressed-tensors test due to a support predicate, without evidence of a production kernel behavior failure. I treated it as a test/CI-oriented fix rather than a confirmed kernel-correctness case.

DP attention with breakable prefill CUDA graphs fabricated dummy EXTEND batches but built decode metadata, making sparse prefill assert on idle ranks. A full DP/breakable-CUDA-graph serving test with idle ranks would plausibly expose it.

The record says DeepEP BF16 compatibility failed when launching a DeepSeek-style GLM model and the fix is in the EP MoE layer. An end-to-end DeepEP BF16 launch test for that model family would plausibly catch the issue, though the exact root cause is not fully shown.

The fused quant layernorm tests exposed int8/fp8 precision errors and an illegal memory access when scale_ub was unset. Unit tests sweeping scale_ub and quantized dtypes against a reference would plausibly catch the failures.

A TRT-LLM MoE routing-method regression made Nemotron FP8 deployment unsupported and required routing-method fixes for several NVIDIA MoE models. NVIDIA backend CI over those model/quantization combinations would plausibly catch the bad routing gate.
The ApplyTokenBitmaskInplace CUDA kernel needed to compile only on CUDA 12.4 or newer. A CUDA-version build matrix for sgl-kernel would plausibly detect the unsupported compile path.

The record only says modelopt weight-load compatibility for a different pack method was fixed, without a visible crash, wrong output, or kernel-specific root cause. I could not confidently classify it as a kernel-correctness fix.

The PR is described as solving a CUDA 11.8 issue for CUTLASS MLA and modifies kernel build workflows plus the CUTLASS MLA kernel. A CUDA 11.8 build/run matrix for that kernel would plausibly catch the compatibility failure.

The AMD AITER backend missed required k_scale/v_scale arguments for non-MLA speculative paths and crashed with a TypeError in ROCm nightly. ROCm CI covering Qwen3-Coder-Next speculative decoding on AITER would plausibly catch it.

The DSV4.1 Flash Gluon kernel used a Triton API that changed in Triton 3.8, causing an import error in the CUDA 13.4 nightly image. A compiler/container matrix including Triton 3.8 would plausibly catch the incompatibility.
The CPU extension applied x86-only flags and FP16 vector types on Power Architecture, causing build failures. A Power build job for CPU kernels would plausibly catch the architecture-specific break.

The DeepSeek-V2.5-1210-FP8 model could not deploy and failed while initializing the FP8 Cutlass MoE path. An end-to-end serve/init smoke test for that model and EP/TP configuration would plausibly expose the crash.
